title: Etale algebraic spaces descend along separated universal homeomorphisms
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $r:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume that $X$ and $Y$ are quasi-separated: their absolute diagonals over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ are quasi-compact on scheme tests, where quasi-compact for a scheme morphism means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Assume that $r$ is separated, meaning that its diagonal is a representable closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and that for every algebraic space $T\to Y$ the map $|X\times_YT|\to|T|$ is a homeomorphism. For an algebraic space $H$, let $\operatorname{Et}(H)$ be the category of chartwise etale morphisms $E\to H$ from quasi-separated algebraic spaces and all morphisms over $H$. Chartwise etale means that after composing with any representable etale scheme chart of $E$ the resulting map to $H$ is representable etale, with scheme etaleness as in [def-weil-etale-morphism]; $E\to H$ itself need not be representable. Let $\operatorname{Et}_{\mathrm{sep}}(H)$ be the full subcategory whose objects have closed-immersion relative diagonal. Then base change along $r$ induces equivalences
$$\operatorname{Et}(Y)\simeq\operatorname{Et}(X),\qquad \operatorname{Et}_{\mathrm{sep}}(Y)\simeq\operatorname{Et}_{\mathrm{sep}}(X).$$
In particular every separated etale object over $X$ is isomorphic over $X$ to the pullback of a separated etale object over $Y$.

source.place: Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of etale morphisms, author version 2010-03-03, Theorem (5.21), printed p.24, including its E_sep restriction; quasi-separated convention on printed p.4. Author PDF read at https://davidrydh.se/papers/submersion20100305.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every base change of $r$ has a homeomorphic point map, hence is open and surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-space-open-surjection-etale-descent] to $p=r$: the functor $\operatorname{Et}(Y)\to\operatorname{Desc}(r)$ is an equivalence. In particular the pullback objects are quasi-separated and chartwise etale. It remains to show that forgetting the datum is an equivalence $\operatorname{Desc}(r)\to\operatorname{Et}(X)$, and to check the separated subcategories.

Put $X_2=X\times_YX$ and $d=\Delta_r:X\to X_2$. Its first projection $p_1:X_2\to X$ is a base change of $r$, so its point map is a homeomorphism. Since $p_1d=\mathrm{id}$, the continuous point map of $d$ is its inverse. The assumed separatedness makes $d$ a representable closed immersion. It is therefore a thickening. By [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change] every base change of $d$ is a thickening. On scheme tests these are scheme universal homeomorphisms, so [lem-trf-universally-homeomorph-integral] makes them integral, universally injective and surjective. Consequently [lem-sfb-space-integral-radicial-etale-invariance] applies to $d$ and to every base change of $d$: their pullback functors on all chartwise etale algebraic spaces are fully faithful (indeed equivalences). The fibre products and the continuous point maps used here are supplied by the cited space-calculus statements.

source.place: Theorem (5.21), diagonal nil-immersion; Stacks 05ZH for its etale invariance

proof.text: For $V\in\operatorname{Et}(X)$, the two objects $p_1^*V,p_2^*V$ over $X_2$ are chartwise etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Their pullbacks along $d$ are both $V$. Full faithfulness from step 2 uniquely lifts $\mathrm{id}_V$ to a morphism $\theta_V:p_1^*V\to p_2^*V$; lifting the reverse identity shows it is invertible, since the composites restrict to identities and pullback is faithful. It is normalized by construction. Over $X_3=X\times_YX\times_YX$, pull back the proposed cocycle identity along $e:X_2\to X_3$, $(x,z)\mapsto(x,x,z)$. This is a base change of $d$, so step 2 gives faithful pullback along $e$. Under $e$, $\theta_{12}$ is the identity and both $\theta_{23}$ and $\theta_{13}$ become $\theta_V$. Thus the two composites agree after $e$ and hence before $e$. This constructs a normalized cocycle for every $V$; any normalized cocycle must equal this one by faithfulness along $d$.

source.place: Theorem (5.21), unique descent datum; expanded normalization and triple-overlap check

proof.text: Every $X$-morphism $a:V\to W$ respects the constructed data. Indeed the maps $p_2^*a\circ\theta_V$ and $\theta_W\circ p_1^*a$ both pull back along $d$ to $a$, so they agree by full faithfulness in step 2. Thus the forgetful functor from $\operatorname{Desc}(r)$ has exactly one datum over each object and all the morphisms of $\operatorname{Et}(X)$; its inverse assigns $V\mapsto(V,\theta_V)$. Composing with the effective-descent equivalence of step 1 gives precisely the claimed base-change equivalence $\operatorname{Et}(Y)\simeq\operatorname{Et}(X)$.

source.place: Theorems (5.19)(i), (5.21), full faithfulness and essential surjectivity

proof.text: Separatedness is preserved by pullback: a scheme test of the new diagonal is a base change of a scheme test of the old diagonal, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] applies. To reflect it, let $g:E\to Y$ be an etale object and suppose $E_X\to X$ is separated. For any algebraic space $T\to E\times_YE$, put $D=E\times_{E\times_YE}T$ and $T'=T\times_YX$. The pullback $D'=D\times_YX\to T'$ is a base change of $\Delta_{E_X/X}$, hence a closed immersion and universally closed by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper]. The vertical maps $D'\to D$ and $T'\to T$ are base changes of $r$, hence homeomorphisms on point spaces. The point map $|D|\to|T|$ is the conjugate of the closed map $|D'|\to|T'|$, so is closed. This holds for every $T$, proving universal closedness of $\Delta_g$. Now [lem-sfb-space-separated-diagonal-closed] implies that $g$ is separated. Therefore the equivalence restricts to the full separated subcategories: a preimage of a separated object is separated by reflection, and the same bijections on morphisms apply. The final existence assertion is its essential surjectivity.
